title: Why B2B SaaS is the best startup model: recurring revenue, vertical niches, 2/20/200 validation, and AI
summary: Rob Walling argues B2B SaaS is the most repeatable, bootstrappable startup model thanks to recurring revenue, high margins and strong exit multiples. He explains vertical vs horizontal vs orthogonal SaaS, his 2/20/200 validation framework, net negative churn, and why AI is a feature rather than a threat.

principles.text: Recurring revenue is the core appeal of SaaS: you stop starting every month from zero.
principles.quote: SAS is incredible because it's recurring revenue.

principles.text: B2B SaaS is less luck-dependent than marketplaces or consumer apps because there are repeatable rules of thumb.
principles.quote: B2B SAS is boring, but much higher likelihood of success if you're kind of following some rules of thumb or best practices.

principles.text: Know exactly who your customer is and where they are; that is why vertical and orthogonal SaaS beat horizontal.
principles.quote: the idea of knowing who your customer is and where they are is such a huge advantage in any B2B SAS. And this is why horizontal SAS is harder.

principles.text: High SaaS margins mean you can bootstrap, and recurring high-margin revenue earns the best exit multiples.
principles.quote: SAS at scale you can see 80 to 90% gross margins and 30 to 50% net margins on SAS.

principles.text: Validate demand cheaply before building: 2 hours of research, 20 hours of landing page and outreach, then 200 hours for an MVP.
principles.quote: there's a lot of developers building a lot of in their basement for 6 months that nobody wants

principles.text: Prefer businesses where AI is a feature, not the whole product, so you keep a moat without it.
principles.quote: we have tended to fund where AI is a feature. You still have a moat without AI.
